messages.message: ### Step 2: Direct Translation Translate each source line into Bengali, guided by the Reference Translation and Step 1 analysis. Output: ONE Bengali line per source line (preserve line count and end punctuation). Rules: - Follow the meaning from Reference Translation. - For "so X that Y": keep resultative structure, do NOT convert to "because". - No internal punctuation; copy only end punctuation from source.
এবং তিনি আমার মুখের সামনে থেকে না সরলেন, বরং তিনি আমার পথকে এত বাধা দিলেন যে, ফিরতে আমি বারবার ঘুরে গিয়েছিলাম।

### Step 3: Word Table & Coverage Check Build a word table from Step 2 translation, mapping each source word to its target equivalent. Output: ONE Markdown table (all lines combined). Columns: [Source Word] | [Contextual Definition] | [Target Word/Phrase] | [Back-Translation] | [Status: OK/MISSING/WRONG/GRAMMAR/UNNECESSARY] Mark GRAMMAR for agreement errors (gender, number, case) or other grammatical mistakes. Mark UNNECESSARY for elements present in source but not needed in target language (e.g., articles that target language omits naturally). After the table, list any MISSING, WRONG, GRAMMAR, or UNNECESSARY items.

**Word‑to‑Word Alignment Table**
| Source Word | Contextual Definition (from Step 1) | Target Word / Phrase (Bengali) | Back‑Translation (EN) | Status | |-------------|--------------------------------------|--------------------------------|------------------------|--------| | e | coordinating conjunction linking clauses | এবং | “and” | OK | | non | negation of the predicate | না | “not” | OK | | mi | female participant (subject) | তিনি | “she” (formal) | OK | | si | reflexive clitic (part of *partia*) | — | — | UNNECESSARY | | partia | move (intransitive) | সরলেন | “moved” (past polite) | OK | | dinanzi | spatial “in front of” | সামনে | “in front” | OK | | al | preposition + definite article “to the” | — | — | UNNECESSARY | | volto | “face” (object of spatial relation) | মুখের | “of the face” | OK | | anzi | contrastive adverb “nay, rather” | বরং | “rather” | OK | | ’mpediva | hinder (verb) | বাধা দিলেন | “hindered” | OK | | tanto | degree intensifier “so” | এত | “so” | OK | | il | definite article | — | — | UNNECESSARY | | mio | possessive “my” | আমার | “my” | OK | | cammino | “road, path” (object of hindrance) | পথকে | “road (ACC)” | OK | | ch’ | subordinating conjunction “that” | যে | “that” | OK | | i’ | first‑person pronoun “I” | আমি | “I” | OK | | fui | past‑historic copula “was / had” | গিয়েছিলাম | “had gone” (auxiliary) | OK | | per | purpose preposition “for, in order to” | — | — | UNNECESSARY | | ritornar | infinitive “to return” | ফিরতে | “to return” | OK | | più | comparative adverb indicating frequency “more” | বারবার | “oftentimes / repeatedly” | OK | | volte | noun “times” (frequency) | — | — | UNNECESSARY | | vòlto | verb “turned” | ঘুরে | “turned” | OK |

### Items Requiring Attention - **UNNECESSARY**: `si`, `al`, `il`, `per`, `volte` – these elements are not overtly expressed in Bengali and are naturally omitted. - **MISSING / WRONG / GRAMMAR**: none.

### Step 4: Correction & Final Output Fix any MISSING, WRONG, or GRAMMAR items from Step 3. Reorder within line if needed; do not add new content words. Verify that the output contains only Bengali script; no other language scripts should be mixed in. Output format (use nested bullet list, not table): - Line N: - Original: ... - Issue: ... (or "none") - Corrected: ... (or "no change") Output final Bengali text in ONE code block, line by line (no extra prose).
